Below is a quick‑look table of the **federal statutory holidays that create “long weekends”** in Canada for the calendar year 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a Monday or Friday, the adjacent weekend is automatically part of a three‑day break. If it falls on a weekend, the holiday is observed on the following Monday, which also produces a long weekend that includes the weekend *before* the holiday.)

| Holiday (Federal) | Date in 2023 | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Days (inclusive) |
|-------------------|--------------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| New Year’s Day (observed) | **Jan 2** | Mon | Dec 30–31 (2022) & Jan 2 |
| Family Day (Ontario) | **Feb 20** | Mon | Feb 18–19 & Feb 20 |
| Good Friday | **Apr 7** | Fri | Apr 7–8–9 |
| Victoria Day | **May 24** | Mon | May 22–23 & May 24 |
| Canada Day (observed) | **Jul 3** | Mon | Jul 1–2 & Jul 3 |
| Labour Day | **Sep 4** | Mon | Sep 2–3 & Sep 4 |
| Thanksgiving | **Oct 9** | Mon | Oct 7–8 & Oct 9 |
| Remembrance Day | **Nov 11** | Fri | Nov 11–12–13 |
| Christmas Day | **Dec 25** | Mon | Dec 23–24 & Dec 25 |
| Boxing Day | **Dec 26** | Tue | Dec 25–26–27 (the weekend after is Dec 30–31) |

> **Note:**  
> • Some provinces have additional holidays that also create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. George’s Day in Prince Edward Island, etc.).  
> • The table above lists only the federal holidays that affect the entire country.  

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app! If you need the provincial‑specific long weekends, let me know and I can compile those as well.
